headline: FED HIKE ODDS JUMP TO 94% — Gold Holds $3,888 Monday as Markets Await Warsh Signals Ahead of Retail Sales and FOMC Minutes
snippet: Gold edged to $3,888/oz Monday as CME FedWatch lifted the implied probability of a December 25-basis-point rate hike to 94%, up from 85% last week, after Governor Bowman's November 11 inflation comments hardened the Fed's hawkish posture. Markets are parsing comments from new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh for any hint of a pivot, with two critical data points this week providing the clearest test of the $3,800 support level identified by CPM Group: US retail sales on Tuesday and FOMC minutes on Wednesday. Even a split vote in those minutes could drag December hike odds back toward 65-70% and spark a relief rally toward $4,000.

headline: PALADIN ENERGY LAUNCHES A$525M RAISE FOR PATTERSON LAKE SOUTH — World's No. 2 Listed Uranium Miner Targets Saskatchewan First Production in 2031
snippet: Paladin Energy has launched an A$525 million (C$511M) equity raise to advance its Patterson Lake South uranium project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin toward first production in 2031. The capital raise comes with uranium spot holding near $90.41/lb and long-term utility contracts benchmarking at a record US$99/lb — the highest TradeTech has recorded since it began publishing the series in 1996 — giving Paladin a compelling margin story to pitch to institutional investors on the raise.

headline: LOTUS SHIPS FIRST 145,000 LB OF URANIUM FROM MALAWI — Kayelekera Milestone Cargo Bound for France's Orano, 173,000 lb Off-Spec Ore Sold to US Buyer
snippet: Lotus Resources (ASX: LOT) has dispatched its first commercial uranium shipment from the Kayelekera mine in Malawi — approximately 145,000 pounds of U₃O₈ in four containers bound for Orano CE Malvesi in France — marking the company's first revenue milestone following mine restart. Lotus also separately sold 173,000 lbs of off-specification ore inventory to a US-listed global critical minerals company, monetising material that had been flagged for higher product impurities. Kayelekera is one of the few new uranium mines to reach commercial production in 2026 outside of Kazakhstan and Canada.

headline: KINROSS FACES CLASS ACTION OVER SURPRISE 2026 OUTPUT CUT — Shareholders Sue Over Guidance Slash From 2.0 Moz to 1.84-1.86 Moz
snippet: Law firm Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz filed a class action against Kinross Gold (NYSE: KGC) on November 15 on behalf of shareholders who purchased KGC between February 18 and September 23, 2026. The claim alleges Kinross misled investors about its ability to meet 2.0 million gold-equivalent-ounce annual production guidance, then slashed that target to 1.84-1.86 million ounces in a September mid-quarter update that sent the stock down 5.8% on November 10 when broader sector weakness compounded the news. The lawsuit is at allegation stage and Kinross has not yet responded publicly.

headline: PAN AMERICAN SILVER SELLS MANANTIAL ESPEJO TO CERRADO GOLD — Argentine Mine Exit Continues Majors' November Asset Rotation Into Mid-Tiers
snippet: Pan American Silver has divested the past-producing Manantial Espejo silver-gold mine in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, to Cerrado Gold on an "as is, where is" basis, the sixth meaningful mining M&A deal in the past 10 days. The move continues Pan American's strategic concentration into higher-tier assets including LAC and San Rafael, while Cerrado gains a past-producing operation in a province adjacent to its Minera Don Nicolás operations — a consolidation play in a jurisdiction it already understands.

headline: YANGSHAN COPPER IMPORT PREMIUM HITS RECORD $285/T — China Scrambles for Physical Metal Even as LME Price Sits Near 4-Month Low
snippet: The Yangshan copper import premium — a real-time measure of China's physical metal appetite — hit a record US$285 a tonne last week even as the LME three-month contract dropped to $13,358, its lowest since mid-July. Shanghai Futures Exchange copper inventories fell 18.3% week-on-week to 27,642 tonnes, the tightest since December 2023. The divergence between weak financial-market pricing (driven by AI-equity selling since the US midterm elections) and exceptionally tight physical conditions in China is the most striking macro copper signal in this correction cycle.

headline: ZACKS NAMES 4 GOLD STOCKS TO WEATHER THE CORRECTION — Fury Gold, Gold Royalty, Newmont and B2Gold Lead for Balance Sheet Strength at $3,884 Gold
snippet: Zacks Investment Research identifies Fury Gold Mines, Gold Royalty Corp, Newmont Corporation and B2Gold as four gold producers positioned to outperform through the current correction, citing strong balance sheets and growth pipelines that remain margin-positive at current gold prices. The analysis highlights Newmont's Tanami expansion as the standout catalyst: expected to add 150,000-200,000 ounces of annual production while reducing operating costs by approximately 30%, a margin improvement that becomes structurally significant if gold settles into a $3,800-$4,000 range rather than recovering to its January highs.

headline: KITCO OPINION: IS $3,800 GOLD'S LAST LINE? — CPM Group Maps What Retail Sales and FOMC Minutes Must Show to Keep the Floor Intact
snippet: In a November 13 Kitco commentary, CPM Group's market strategist argues that $3,800 is the critical support level where gold's 8-month ascending pattern is tested in earnest — with the December Fed rate hike priced at 94% probability, a 5.15% 10-year Treasury yield, and the dollar at a 19-month peak all compressing gold's opportunity cost. The piece frames three variables that determine whether this is a buying opportunity or the opening of a deeper bear phase: the December FOMC decision itself, the trajectory of the 10-year yield, and whether $3,800 holds on a weekly close basis. Silver's equivalent line is pegged at $45-$48, where financial-market selling would begin to intersect structural industrial demand from solar manufacturers.
